tests/presentation/components/test_mesh_.fixture_review: Checked tests/presentation/components/mesh_support.py (FakeMeshScene/FakeMeshCamera/FakeMeshRenderer/FakePickingMeshRenderer/FakeMeshSignal/FailingInitializationRenderer) and the module-local _Renderer/_Signal/_Screen/_Window/_Timer doubles against production mesh_view.py. Fakes mirror the native Scene/Camera/Renderer surface actually called by OpenGLViewer (scene.clear/add_mesh/empty/get_bounds/selection, camera.reset/show_object/restore_state/rotate/pan/has_velocity, renderer.suspend/resume/clear_frame/set_plan_texture/pick). _make_page_plane_viewer builds an OpenGLViewer via __new__ and sets every attribute the exercised paths read; added a scene_content_changed recorder there so emissions are observable. Real native ost_renderer.Camera/MeshData/Box3 are used where inertia and mesh conversion matter. The three real-widget classes create real Qt windows and patch only _ensure_renderer. Found a real fixture defect: MeshViewNativeSurfaceOwnerTests never created a QApplication (it ran first alphabetically), so running the module alone hard-crashed the interpreter (0xC0000409) instead of failing; fixed by creating the app in the test and dropping the cross-test import of tests.integration.selection.area_routing_support. Found a swallowed-AssertionError pattern (patch side_effect=AssertionError inside code guarded by except Exception) in cleanup test; replaced by assert_not_called. Ran ~70 single-line production mutations against the module (script in scratchpad); remaining survivors are equivalent/defense-in-depth lines (redundant hidden-surface guards layered with resume_rendering, disconnect-then-connect dedupe, accepted-bid None check subsumed by the != check), timer disconnect hygiene in cleanup, and setters/wheel/delete-key paths outside the assigned tests.
